top_story: A deadly Houthi strike and a subsequent projectile impact at Riyadh’s King Khalid airport on 11 October signaled a sharper Yemen war spillover into Saudi urban infrastructure, heightening pressure on civilians, travel, and the kingdom’s sense of internal security. That same day, a migrant boat carrying 305 people capsized off Djibouti en route to Yemen, leaving at least 139 dead and 84 missing, exposing how the war’s wider instability keeps driving desperate movement into one of the region’s most dangerous corridors. In Gaza, accounts published on 12-13 October from Israeli intelligence personnel and soldiers described a recent shift toward looser targeting standards and the killing of unarmed Palestinians later labeled as militants, deepening evidence that permissive rules are shaping the war’s human toll. Together, these developments show regional conflicts not only intensifying militarily but also normalizing practices that push civilians into lethal exposure by air, at sea, and under occupation.
